tasks.short: Check a quote or invoice against the rate card and add overhead.

today.trigger: A supplier quote, a customer job estimate, or an invoice that does not match the agreed price arrives by mail or in AFAS Profit.
steps: Open the quotation or price list from Outlook or SharePoint and the matching article or purchase contract in AFAS.
Type quantities, rates, fuel or peak surcharges and the overhead key into Excel.
Compare the total with the supplier invoice or the amount the site wants to charge.
Ask the buyer or the site when a line has no agreed rate, including flex hours from the staffing agencies.
File the sheet and, where needed, correct the cost price in AFAS.
drudgery: Retyping a rate card from a PDF into Excel
Hunting the current fuel surcharge and the right site price list
Recalculating agency hours against the agreed rate and the CAO inlenersbeloning
today.time_sinks: Most of the time goes to finding the current price and retyping lines. The arithmetic itself is short.

lenses.faster: Reading the quote and extending quantity, rate, surcharge and overhead drops out of the job. The bookkeeper opens only the lines that have no contract price or that sit outside the agreed difference.
lenses.autonomous: A supplier invoice posted in AFAS, or a quote landing in the AP mailbox, starts the pricing run on its own. Nobody has to remember to do the batch on Friday.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost Noordhaven would price every warehouse job and every agency hour against the contract before payment, across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo. Touchless invoices would then include a price check, which they do not today.
lenses.joy: Retyping price lists is the part nobody will miss. Agreeing an odd surcharge with a site manager is the part worth keeping.
lenses.options: Each job can show the contract price, the quoted price, and two surcharge scenarios side by side, from the same rate card.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper maintains the rate card, the overhead key and the allowed difference in AFAS, and reviews what falls outside them. The line calculation runs from the contract.
reach: Check staffing-agency invoices against the order and the CAO inlenersbeloning before the payroll specialist or the buyer disputes them
Prepare the purchase-price variance the controller now rebuilds at month close
Hand FP&A a standard cost by site that already ties to the ledger

tasks.human_edge: Knowing which surcharge the Rotterdam site actually agreed, and when a low quote would break the service, is still a conversation with the buyer and the site manager.
tasks.pattern_why: The arithmetic is a rule once the lines exist, but the quote usually arrives as a PDF or a mail. A model turns that into supplier, quantity and price. A rate-card check then accepts or rejects the total, and a person sees the breaks.

in_practice.trigger: A supplier invoice is registered in AFAS, or a quote arrives in the shared AP mailbox.
steps: Read the document into supplier, description, quantity and unit price.
Match each line to the AFAS purchase contract or the current SharePoint rate card for that site.
Extend quantity, agreed rate, surcharge and the overhead key the controller has set.
Update the cost price when the result sits inside the agreed difference.
Leave the line on the exception list, with the reason, when it does not.
in_practice.human_gate: A line with no contract price, a difference above the agreed band, or any agency rate that breaks the inlenersbeloning waits for the bookkeeper before AFAS is changed.
data_needed: Purchase contracts and article cost prices in AFAS
Site rate cards and the current fuel and peak surcharge tables
Agency rate agreements and the CAO pay elements used for inlenersbeloning
The overhead key agreed with the controller
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS cost-price change log, plus the priced quote stored in the SharePoint AP folder for that period.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit stores purchase contracts and article cost prices and can price a coded line from that list.
A PDF quotation can be split into supplier, quantity and price, after which the check is ordinary arithmetic against a rate card.
Dutch agency invoices are often checked against inlenersbeloning and the agreed hourly rate, and that check is tabular once hours and rates are in columns.

risks: A wrong cost price flows into the margin and into customer invoices before the controller sees it.
Quotes from owner-drivers are personal data under the AVG. They should stay in AFAS and SharePoint under the agreements already in place, and not go to a loose external chat tool.
Surcharges written in prose get a confident wrong number when the clause is ambiguous.
A stale rate card underprices flex labour after a CAO wage rise.
research_questions: Last quarter, what share of these calculations started from an AFAS contract or a structured rate card, and what share started from a free-text PDF or mail?
On 30 recent quotations, how often does extraction plus the rate card match the bookkeeper's total within 1 percent?
How many supplier and agency invoices were paid last month at a price different from the contract, and by how much in euros?
Who may change an article cost price in AFAS today, and does anyone review the change?

tasks.short: Match the Rabobank statement to open invoices.

today.trigger: The Rabobank statement arrives, or open items are still uncleared when the bookkeeper opens the bank journal.
steps: Bring the statement into AFAS Profit.
Accept the matches AFAS suggests on amount, IBAN and payment reference.
Manually link the rest: one payment covering many invoices, partial payments, and lines with no reference.
Ask the customer, the agency or the site for a remittance when a line will not match.
Book bank costs, interest and the lines that are not invoices.
drudgery: Clicking through lines that almost matched
Splitting one customer receipt across many open invoices
Copying a remittance from mail into the match screen
today.time_sinks: The unmatched tail takes the time, especially customers who pay several invoices in one transfer and leave out the betalingskenmerk.

lenses.faster: Importing the statement and posting the clean matches drops out of the morning. What remains is splitting combined payments and booking lines that are not invoices.
lenses.autonomous: Each new Rabobank statement starts the match as soon as the file is in AFAS. The bookkeeper opens an exception list, not a blank bank journal.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost every statement would be matched the same morning, with a running figure for unexplained cash the controller can use before month end. That shortens the close and shows days sales outstanding on money that has already arrived.
lenses.joy: Ticking a payment that is obviously the same invoice is the part that goes. Deciding that a customer short-paid on purpose still belongs with credit and collections.
lenses.options: Each unmatched line can show the three closest open items and the field that favoured each one.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper tunes the match rules, the reference formats and the allowed date window, and clears a daily queue. The statement match itself runs from those rules.
reach: Do the first pass of cash application that now waits for the credit and collections officer
Give the controller a same-day unexplained-cash figure for the cash forecast
Spot a duplicate supplier payment before the Rabobank payment batch is released

tasks.human_edge: Deciding that a short payment is a dispute, an agreed discount, or a mistake still needs the contract and, often, the customer relationship the credit officer holds.
tasks.pattern_why: Amount, IBAN, invoice number and the Dutch payment reference are structured fields. The match is a rule with three outcomes: post, suggest, or leave. A model is not required to do the match.

in_practice.trigger: A Rabobank statement file is received in AFAS.
steps: Match each line on amount, IBAN, invoice number and betalingskenmerk inside the agreed date window.
Post the matches that meet the rule.
Propose up to three open items when one receipt covers several invoices or a partial amount.
Leave bank costs, interest and unknown counterparties on the exception list with the statement text.
in_practice.human_gate: Anything the rule does not clear waits for the bookkeeper. A write-off or a cash discount is not posted from the match rule.
data_needed: Rabobank statement lines with IBAN, amount, date and reference
Open purchase and sales items in AFAS
Customer and supplier IBANs on the master records
Remittance mails in the shared AP and AR mailbox
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS bank-match log, so each Rabobank line shows the rule that cleared it or the person who matched it.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit matches bank lines to open items on amount, account and payment reference and can post the matches that meet the rule.
Rabobank delivers statement files that a Dutch ledger can import without retyping each line.
Combined customer payments with a weak reference remain a common manual match in Dutch accounts receivable.

risks: A loose rule clears the wrong invoice and hides a real short payment, which flatters days sales outstanding.
An agency batch paid with one reference gets booked to suspense, or matched to the wrong week, and the flex-worker invoice stays open.
A rule that ignores duplicates will clear a second payment of the same invoice.
research_questions: Last month, what percentage of Rabobank lines did AFAS match on its own, and what percentage did a bookkeeper match by hand?
Of the hand matches, how many were combined payments, missing references, bank costs, or something else?
How many automatic matches were undone in the last two quarters?
Does the nightly AFAS extract already contain the unmatched bank balance, so Power BI could show it each morning?

tasks.short: Pull the cash, AP, AR and result tables for the close.

today.trigger: The controller, a site manager, the auditor, or the monthly close asks for a table that is not already on the Power BI dashboard.
steps: Export cash receipts, AP, AR or the profit and loss from AFAS to Excel.
Cut it by site, Rotterdam, Tilburg or Venlo, and by age or ledger.
Check the total to the general ledger.
Format the sheet and mail it, or drop it on SharePoint.
Rebuild a near-copy later because the file was never saved as a standard report.
drudgery: Repeating the same export and pivot every week
Repairing columns when an AFAS export layout shifts
Proving a spreadsheet total that does not match the ledger
today.time_sinks: Reformatting the export and proving it ties to AFAS takes longer than reading the figures.

lenses.faster: The export, the pivot and the tie to the ledger are already done when the bookkeeper opens the pack. Assembling the workbook drops out.
lenses.autonomous: The nightly AFAS extract refreshes the cash, AP, AR and result tables before the office opens. Nobody starts Excel to produce the standard set.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost every site would have a daily AP and AR pack that ties to the ledger, and the auditor would take samples from that same source. Audit adjustments would start from one set of figures.
lenses.joy: Rebuilding last week's workbook is the part that goes. Explaining a real swing in overdue debt to a site manager is the part worth keeping.
lenses.options: The same pack can show the figures by site, by customer group and by age bucket from one refresh.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper decides which cuts are standard and which movements deserve a look, and keeps the tie-out definition current. The table is a refresh of the ledger.
reach: Produce the actuals extract the FP&A analysts now copy out of AFAS
Prepare the recurring audit tables the accountants rebuild at year end
Give the credit and collections officer an AR aging that already matches the ledger

tasks.human_edge: Seeing whether a variance is a story the business should hear, or a coding error between two sites, still takes a bookkeeper who knows how the invoices were booked.
tasks.pattern_why: Cash receipts, payables, receivables and the result are balances in AFAS. A table that ties to the ledger is a query with a check total. Power BI already refreshes an AFAS extract every night, so a model is not the missing piece.

in_practice.trigger: The nightly AFAS extract finishes, or a named close report hits its place on the calendar.
steps: Refresh the standard cash, AP, AR and result tables from the extract.
Tie each total to the trial balance and mark any difference.
Publish the tied tables to the finance Power BI workspace and the close folder.
Leave a one-off cut, or any table that does not tie, on a request list for the bookkeeper.
in_practice.human_gate: A table that ties to the trial balance can refresh on its own. A new cut, or any total that does not tie, is not sent to a site or the auditor until a bookkeeper has looked at it.
data_needed: Nightly AFAS finance extract with ledger, site, open item and due date
A fixed list of standard reports and the ledger accounts each one includes
The trial-balance total for the same period
in_practice.logs_to: The Power BI dataset refresh history, with the tie-out result stored next to the report in the SharePoint close folder.

evidence.claim: Power BI scheduled refresh can publish AP, AR, cash and profit-and-loss tables from a nightly ledger extract.
AFAS Profit produces open-item lists, aging and financial statements from the same ledger as the trial balance.
Where a standard dashboard already exists, the remaining bookkeeper time sits in one-off cuts and in proving that a spreadsheet still matches the ledger.

risks: A table that refreshes itself will be trusted even when it has stopped tying to the ledger.
Site managers keep a private Excel copy, and the close then has two totals.
Auditor requests that do not match a standard cut still need someone who knows the ledger codes.
research_questions: Which of cash receipts, AP aging, AR aging and result by site already exist in Power BI and are actually used?
How many hours last month did the three bookkeepers spend exporting AFAS to Excel for these tables?
Do the dashboard totals match the AFAS trial balance with no manual bridge?
What share of requests in the last quarter were repeats of a report that already exists?

tasks.short: Run the trial balance and see what does not tie.

today.trigger: Month close starts, or the accountant or the auditor asks for a period to be signed off.
steps: Check that purchase, sales, bank and payroll journals for the period are posted in AFAS.
Run the trial balance and compare AP, AR and the Rabobank balance with their control accounts.
Investigate suspense, VAT and other accounts that look wrong.
Post corrections and run the balance again.
Send the balance to the controller or put it in the close folder on SharePoint.
drudgery: Re-running the balance after every small correction
Ticking accounts with no list of what changed since yesterday
Copying the balance into the close workbook
today.time_sinks: Finding why a control account does not match its subledger takes the time. Producing the balance itself is already a report in AFAS.

lenses.faster: The balance and the list of accounts that do not tie are ready when the bookkeeper starts. Re-running and copying the report drops out.
lenses.autonomous: On the close calendar the trial balance and the tie-out list are produced once the last scheduled journal has posted. The controller does not have to chase for the first version.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost Noordhaven would keep the tie-outs running all month, so the first day of the close confirms a balance that has been agreeing with the subledgers. That is the direct route to fewer days to close and fewer audit adjustments.
lenses.joy: Copying the same balance into the close file is the part that goes. Finding a real misposting and fixing the cause is the part worth keeping.
lenses.options: The close pack can show the balance before and after proposed corrections, and split by site, before anyone posts.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper owns the tie-out rules: subledger to control, Rabobank to the bank account, VAT accounts to the draft return. The balance is the output of those rules.
reach: Run the first-pass close checklist the controller now chases by mail
Prepare the balance-sheet lead schedules the accountants rebuild
Tell FP&A which accounts are still moving before they lock the forecast

tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a suspense balance is a timing difference or a lost invoice still depends on knowing what the three sites booked that week.
tasks.pattern_why: A trial balance is the sum of posted journals. Debits equal credits, the subledger equals the control account, and the bank equals the Rabobank statement. Each of those is a rule with a pass or a fail.

in_practice.trigger: The close calendar reaches the trial-balance step, after bank import and the payroll journal have a scheduled arrival time.
steps: Produce the trial balance for the period from posted AFAS journals.
Run the tie-outs: AP, AR, bank, VAT and suspense.
List accounts that moved beyond a set amount, or that fail a tie-out.
Hold correcting entries on that list until a bookkeeper posts them.
Mark the period ready for the controller only when the tie-outs pass.
in_practice.human_gate: The balance and the break list can be produced unattended. A correcting journal, and the note that the period is ready for the controller, stays with the bookkeeper.
data_needed: Posted journals for the period, including the payroll journal from the payroll specialist
Subledger totals for AP and AR
The Rabobank balance for the same date
VAT account totals that will feed the return
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS period record and a SharePoint close checklist that notes who reviewed each break.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit produces a trial balance from posted journals for a chosen period.
Comparing a control account with its subledger can be run as a check on the same ledger, and the failures listed.
In a company that already posts in an integrated ledger, the hours on this task sit mainly in investigating breaks, not in computing the balance.

risks: A green 'in balance' flag can hide the difference on a suspense account.
An automatic correction that tidies the symptom will post again next month.
A trial balance that runs before the payroll journal arrives looks finished and is not, which brings the close back later.
research_questions: In the last close, how many hours went to producing the trial balance, and how many to investigating breaks?
Which tie-outs are still manual today: bank, AP, AR, VAT, payroll control?
How many journals hit the period after the first trial balance was sent to the controller?
Does AFAS already warn when a control account differs from its subledger?

tasks.short: Put actuals and the last budget into one pack.

today.trigger: FP&A or the controller asks for budget input, a forecast refresh, or a comparison with last year.
steps: Export actuals by ledger and site from AFAS, and open the previous budget file on SharePoint.
Paste the figures into the budget workbook and repair broken links.
Add a simple run-rate and the year-to-date variance.
Send the pack to the FP&A analysts and answer questions about odd ledger codes.
Cut it again when a site wants only Rotterdam, or warehouse labour split from transport.
drudgery: Copying actuals into a workbook only one person understands
Retieing the pack to the ledger after every paste
Rebuilding the same variance columns each month
today.time_sinks: Making the file tie to AFAS, and then cutting it a second way for a site, takes longer than reading the variance.

lenses.faster: The export, the paste and the tie to the ledger drop out. The bookkeeper checks unusual codes and hands over a pack that already balances.
lenses.autonomous: Once the trial balance for the month is stable, the actuals-versus-budget pack refreshes for all three sites. FP&A does not send a reminder to start the copy.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost the company would keep a monthly bridge from the last budget to the current figures, by site and by cost type, including the seasonal swing in flex hours. That is the pack a forecast the business trusts is built on.
lenses.joy: Maintaining the private workbook is the part that goes. Explaining a real cost spike to a site manager can stay, and it sits closer to FP&A than to booking.
lenses.options: The same actuals can sit under a base, a high-volume and a low-volume view of warehouse labour and flex hours, for FP&A to choose from.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper keeps the mapping from ledger account and site to budget line, and checks it when the chart of accounts changes. The monthly pack is a refresh of that mapping.
reach: Prepare the first-cut actuals pack the FP&A analysts now build in Excel
Split flex-labour cost by agency for the controller, using the staffing invoices already in AP
Give the finance director a site view without a new spreadsheet

tasks.human_edge: Choosing revenue and cost assumptions belongs to FP&A with the business. The bookkeeper's edge is knowing which actual was miscoded and would send the forecast the wrong way.
tasks.pattern_why: Actuals, the prior budget and the site codes are structured data. Compiling them into a pack that ties to the trial balance is a mapping with a check total. The estimate itself stays with FP&A.

in_practice.trigger: The month's trial balance is marked stable on the close checklist.
steps: Refresh actuals by ledger, cost centre and site from AFAS.
Lay them on the budget mapping next to the previous budget and last year.
Flag lines that do not tie to the trial balance, new ledger codes, and large flex-labour swings.
Store the pack on SharePoint with the mapping version and the trial-balance total.
Pass it to FP&A after the bookkeeper confirms the tie.
in_practice.human_gate: FP&A does not lock the forecast on this pack until a bookkeeper has confirmed it ties to the trial balance for that period.
data_needed: AFAS actuals by period, ledger and cost centre
The approved budget and last year's actuals, with a version
The ledger-to-budget-line mapping, split for the transport CAO workforce and the warehouse CAO workforce where the lines differ
A flex-labour total that can be reconciled to agency invoices
in_practice.logs_to: The budget pack in the SharePoint forecast folder, named with the mapping version and the trial-balance total it was tied to.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit reports actuals by period, ledger and cost centre, which is the source of a budget comparison.
Power BI can show actuals against a budget once the budget is loaded into the same model as the nightly finance extract.
After the refresh exists, the remaining errors mostly come from a ledger mapped to the wrong budget line.

risks: A ledger on the wrong budget line makes the forecast look tidy while the sites do not recognise their costs.
Flex headcount moves between about 150 and 300 with the season. A straight run-rate will miss that swing and look precise.
Transport CAO costs and warehouse CAO costs get added together on a headcount split the sites do not use.
research_questions: Is the budget stored in AFAS or only in Excel, and who is allowed to change a budget line?
How many different workbooks did FP&A receive from bookkeeping in the last forecast round?
What share of variance questions were miscoded actuals, and what share were real operational changes?
Can the nightly extract be tied to the trial balance at cost-centre level with no manual bridge?

tasks.short: Update stock quantities and values after the site counts.

today.trigger: A month-end count, a stock difference at a site, or a question about the inventory figure on the balance sheet.
steps: Collect count files from Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo, usually Excel by mail or SharePoint.
Compare quantities with the stock records in AFAS, or with the spreadsheet that stands in for them.
Price the differences at standard cost and look for odd shrink or gains.
Post the adjustment after the site confirms, and check the inventory account on the trial balance.
Chase missing counts, and separate goods that belong to customers from goods Noordhaven owns.
drudgery: Retyping count sheets that arrive in three layouts
Pricing the same slow-moving packaging and spares every month
Chasing the site that sends its file late
today.time_sinks: Waiting for the counts and cleaning the files takes more time than the valuation entry. The hours on this task are already low, about 22 a year per person.

lenses.faster: Retyping counts and extending quantity times standard cost drops out once the file matches the template. The bookkeeper reviews shrink, customer-owned goods, and lines the site disputes.
lenses.autonomous: When a site drops its count file in the agreed SharePoint folder, the comparison with AFAS runs that night and queues the differences. The bookkeeper is not the reminder system.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost Noordhaven would value its own stock, such as packaging, fuel and spares, every week, and keep customer-owned goods off the balance sheet without a month-end scramble.
lenses.joy: Cleaning three different spreadsheets is the part that goes. A straight conversation about a missing cage of packaging at Venlo is the part worth keeping.
lenses.options: Each difference can be shown at standard cost and at last purchase price, with and without the lines the site disputes, before anything is posted.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper sets the count template, the valuation method and the amount that needs a review, and checks the exceptions. Line-by-line stock maintenance runs from the count file and the standard cost.
reach: Give the controller a stock figure that already excludes customer-owned goods
Flag slow-moving packaging and spares for the buyer before more is ordered
Support the accountants on the year-end inventory lead schedule

tasks.human_edge: Deciding whether a difference is shrink, a missed receipt, or goods that were never Noordhaven's takes a conversation with the site. Posting it without that conversation makes the accounts look tidy and wrong.
tasks.pattern_why: With one count template, quantity times standard cost and the tie to the inventory account are rules. Dutch annual accounts need one consistent valuation method, and that method can be written down. A model is only a workaround for sites that refuse the template.

in_practice.trigger: A site saves its count file in the SharePoint count folder, or the month-end count date is reached.
steps: Check the file against the template: article, location, quantity, and a flag for customer-owned goods.
Compare quantities with AFAS and price the difference at the standard cost.
List shrink and gains above the threshold, and any row that is not in the template.
Post an adjustment only after the bookkeeper and the site have confirmed the list.
Tie the inventory account to the trial balance.
in_practice.human_gate: Every shrink or gain above the threshold, every customer-owned item, and every file that breaks the template waits for the bookkeeper. The site confirms a shrink before it hits the result.
data_needed: A single count template used by all three sites
Standard costs and article codes in AFAS
A marker that separates own stock from customer-owned goods
The inventory account balance on the trial balance
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS inventory journal, with the site count file stored in the same SharePoint period folder.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit can hold stock quantities and standard cost and post an inventory adjustment where the stock module is in use.
A fixed spreadsheet template compared with a ledger quantity is ordinary software, and the check total is the inventory account.
Goods a logistics company stores for customers are not its own stock, and recognising them as assets overstates the balance sheet.

risks: Customer-owned pallets or goods booked as Noordhaven stock overstate assets and will not survive the audit.
Three file layouts mean a loader that guesses columns will value the wrong article.
Changing the valuation method inside a quiet script breaks the consistency the annual accounts require.
A silent write-off hides a warehouse problem the site manager should see.
research_questions: Is Noordhaven's own stock kept in AFAS, in Excel, or in a warehouse system this brief did not name?
What is the balance-sheet value of own stock, and how much of last year's adjustment was shrink rather than late paperwork?
Will Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo submit one count template, and who refuses today?
How are customer-owned goods identified so they cannot be posted to the inventory account?

tasks.short: Prepare the VAT return and check the pension and fund invoices.

today.trigger: The VAT period closes, a pension or social-fund invoice arrives, or the accountant asks for figures for the corporate tax file.
steps: Review the VAT codes on purchase and sales invoices in AFAS, with extra care for transport and warehousing.
Run the draft VAT return and trace odd boxes back to invoices.
Tie pension and sector-fund invoices to the payroll totals the payroll specialist provides.
Submit the VAT return the company is responsible for, and pay the amounts that are due.
Pass the year-end figures, including any VAT corrections, to the accountant for the corporate tax return.
drudgery: Copying box totals into a working paper to prove the return
Chasing invoice coding on cross-border transport after the period has closed
Matching a pension invoice to payroll totals by hand
today.time_sinks: The hours are modest, about 20 a year per person, but a wrong VAT box costs more than the time. The slow part is tracing odd codes, not typing the form.

lenses.faster: Gathering the VAT boxes from the ledger, and tying pension and fund invoices to payroll totals, is done before the review. Reading the exceptions and submitting the return stay with the person.
lenses.autonomous: When the period is closed, a draft VAT return and a tie-out of the fund invoices are waiting. Nothing is sent to the Belastingdienst or a fund until a named person releases it.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost Noordhaven would file a monthly VAT return with a written reason for every odd code, and would catch a wrong transport treatment in the week it was booked. The suppletie would become rare, and the cash forecast would carry a VAT payable figure that finance trusts.
lenses.joy: Copying totals into a portal is the part that goes. Deciding the VAT treatment of a cross-border job is the part worth keeping, because it protects the company.
lenses.options: A disputed flow, such as warehousing against transport, or domestic against intra-EU, can be shown under two treatments with the euros at stake, before anyone files.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper maintains the VAT code rules and the checklist that must pass before filing, and reviews what the checklist flags. Completing each form by hand is the old job.
reach: Prepare the VAT lead schedule the accountants now rebuild for the annual file
Check pension and social-fund invoices against payroll totals before the payroll specialist has to chase them
Give FP&A the VAT payable figure for the cash forecast

tasks.human_edge: The person who submits the return is responsible for it. The call on a transport service that sits between 21 percent, 0 percent and reverse charge stays with someone who can explain it to the accountant and, if asked, to the Belastingdienst.
tasks.pattern_why: AFAS can draft the VAT return from the codes, and pension and fund invoices can be tied to payroll totals. Several sources are involved, and the exceptions are real. Filing is a legal act, so a named person reviews and submits before it counts.

in_practice.trigger: The VAT period closes in AFAS, or a pension or sector-fund invoice is registered.
steps: Build the draft VAT return from the posted VAT codes and list invoices that fail a check, including missing codes and unusual transport rates.
Tie the transport CAO pension invoice and the social-fund invoices to payroll totals. Keep employee-level lines with the payroll specialist.
Show two treatments where a flow is disputed, with the euro difference.
Hand the corporate-tax source pack to the accountant at year end. Do not file that return from this desk.
Submit the VAT return only after the bookkeeper releases it.
in_practice.human_gate: Nothing goes to the Belastingdienst, Pensioenfonds Vervoer, or another fund until the bookkeeper has reviewed the draft and released it. The accountant owns the corporate income tax filing. The payroll specialist keeps the wage-tax return and the Whk premium.
data_needed: VAT codes on purchase and sales invoices for the period
The company's written position on VAT for domestic transport, intra-EU transport, warehousing and reverse charge
Payroll totals for pensionable wage and fund wage, supplied by the payroll specialist
Pension and social-fund invoices for the transport CAO and for the warehouse CAO
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS VAT filing archive for that period, and the pension and fund tie-out stored in the same SharePoint close folder.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit builds the Dutch VAT return from the VAT codes on posted invoices and supports digital filing with the Belastingdienst.
Under the CAO for professional goods transport, pension contributions are billed by Pensioenfonds Vervoer and can be tied to payroll totals.
The person who files a Dutch VAT return remains responsible for its content, including where software prepared the boxes.

risks: A wrong VAT return that is filed unattended leads to a suppletie, belastingrente and, where the error is careless, a fine.
This task's US workers' compensation forms do not exist at Noordhaven. Building them would create a filing the Belastingdienst does not want. The Dutch Whk premium stays with the payroll specialist.
Employee-level pension data pasted into an external model sits outside AFAS and breaches the AVG. If a new tool reads that data, the works council needs to hear about it before it is connected.
Two CAOs mean two pension arrangements. A single template will mix transport drivers and warehouse staff.
research_questions: Which of VAT, the intra-EU sales listing, pension, social funds and corporate tax does this bookkeeper actually file, and which sit with the payroll specialist or the accountant?
How many VAT suppleties were filed in the last two years, and what caused each one?
Are VAT codes on transport and warehousing invoices set in AFAS so a draft return can be rebuilt without a spreadsheet?
Does any file on this desk contain employee-level data, and is that already covered by a processor agreement and a conversation with the works council?

role.altitude: The bookkeeper owns the controls on money in and money out: the rate card, the bank-match rules, the VAT codes, the subledger tie-outs and the close checklist. The day shifts from retyping and ticking to keeping those rules sharp and clearing what they flag, so the controller inherits a ledger that already agrees.
reach: First-pass cash application and short-pay reasons for the credit and collections officer
Actuals packs and the ledger-to-budget mapping for the FP&A analysts
VAT and balance-sheet lead schedules for the accountants
The first-pass close checklist for the controller
A tie-out of staffing-agency invoices and CAO pension invoices against payroll totals, with the payroll specialist
role.ceiling_note: These seven tasks are about 216 hours a year per full-time bookkeeper, roughly 14 percent of the role. Much of that slice is already a report inside AFAS, so the hours left are exceptions, not data entry. The larger limit sits in the rest of accounts payable and receivable, which is not in this list: invoice coding, Rabobank payment batches, and the seasonal wave of invoices for 150 to 300 flex workers. A person still files the VAT return and still approves a stock loss or a write-off. Three sites and two collective agreements put a floor under that exception work. A new platform would be the wrong size for this slice.
skills_to_grow: Writing and testing AFAS match rules, VAT codes and rate-card checks, and proving each rule against last month's exceptions
Dutch VAT on transport and warehousing, including domestic, intra-EU and reverse charge, well enough to challenge a draft return
Close design: which tie-outs must pass before the controller sees the trial balance
Reading a forecast pack well enough to tell FP&A which actual is miscoded
Spotting when a staffing-agency charge breaks the contract or the CAO inlenersbeloning
role.ambitious_version: The three bookkeepers run a desk where Rabobank is matched the same day, supplier and agency invoices are priced against the contract before they are paid, and the trial balance confirms a month that has been tying all along. FP&A receives actuals that already agree with the ledger, the VAT return is a review of flagged codes, and the seasonal flex invoices no longer surprise the close. Their time goes to transport-VAT judgments, agency-invoice disputes, and fixing the rules the sites keep breaking. Days to close fall because the subledgers already agreed.
